newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil real ends off 0.06 pct on lower mini-band.
newsitem.headline: Brazil real ends off 0.06 pct on lower mini-band.

text.p: Brazil's real fell 0.06 percent to close at 1.0201 per dollar in the commercial foreign exchange market after the Central Bank set a weaker mini-band for the currency at 1.020 to 1.025 per dollar, dealers said.
The Central Bank set the new real-dollar mini-band through a buy/sell auction before the open. The previous trade level was set on Tuesday at between 1.0195 and 1.0245 reais to the dollar.

The move continued to keep traders guessing as to how much the Central Bank would lower the mini-band for the entire month of September. In recent months, the Central Bank has been lowering the mini-band 0.6 percent a month.

Central Bank interventions this week have left traders wondering whether the bank will again lower the mini-band by 0.6 percent or possibly slow the pace of real depreciation by dropping it by only 0.5 percent.
So far this month, the Central Bank has lowered the mini-band by 0.4 percent.
In the interbank foreign exchange floating rate market, the real fell 0.04 percent to end at 1.0256 real per dollar.
In the illegal parallel market, the real closed steady at 1.038 real per greenback, traders said.
